The Dallas Cowboys are not playing today — their next game is the big one, Monday Night Football tomorrow night against the Philadelphia Eagles.

The Cowboys (2-4) visit the Eagles (2-4) on Monday, October 26, at 7:15 p.m. CT at Lincoln Financial Field in Philadelphia, airing on ESPN and ABC. Both teams enter tied for second place in the NFC East, and both badly need a win.

Dallas comes in off a 23-13 loss last Sunday at Green Bay, its second straight defeat. The Cowboys trailed 17-0 at halftime — the first time they had been shut out in a first half since November 7, 2021 — and quarterback Dak Prescott threw for one touchdown against two interceptions in Packers territory as Dallas was forced to abandon the run. The defense held Green Bay to 57 rushing yards, but Packers quarterback Jordan Love threw for 276 yards and a touchdown and ran for another score.

Philadelphia is reeling too, after a fourth straight loss, 25-14 to Carolina. The Eagles are without Super Bowl-winning quarterback Jalen Hurts, who is sidelined for the season due to blood clots, leaving Tanner McKee under center. Star wide receiver DeVonta Smith has been ruled out for Monday night with a hamstring injury, and wide receiver Dontayvion Wicks, linebacker Nolan Smith, and cornerback Michael Carter are also out.

History favors Dallas in this rivalry: the Cowboys lead the all-time series 75-59, and the teams split last season, with Philadelphia winning 24-20 in Week 1 and Dallas winning 24-21 in Week 11. Oddsmakers have the Cowboys as 4.5-point favorites on Monday night.

Sources: USA Today Sportsbook Wire, New York Post, Athlon Sports, October 25, 2026.
